reason: Left has cleaner, well-scaled stacked bars with totals, a share chart and a polished decision callout, while right wastes axis range on phone, uses a truncated line chart and unformatted table totals.

Left's colored above/below-target bars with a clear target line and compact phone layout beat right's single-color chart with value labels colliding with the dashed line and a very long card-stacked phone table.
Right has nicer desktop bar charts but clips the 100% axis label and overflows its table on phone, whereas left stays intact at both widths with a clear annotated line chart.
Left's utilization chart with color-coded thresholds and a large legible reroute diagram is much clearer than right's tiny diagram and plain charts, despite left's phone tables clipping.
Left's labeled grouped bars with balances under each category and highlighted table rows are richer and clearer, though its phone table clips, while right's phone chart drops a category label.
Left adds visual structure with stat chips, tinted callouts and a clean table, making the FAQ more scannable than right's plainer cards.
Left reads as a warm, well-typeset letter with a highlighted list and a dated timeline, while right is a plain sectioned bullet document.
Right turns the guide into numbered step cards with a prominent warning, quick facts and checklists that are far more usable than left's sparse bulleted page.
Left's banner header, date badges, reading-progress card and stat tiles give a polished newsletter feel, whereas right is a plain table-and-bullets page.
Right's color-coded price bars, time-of-day timeline and summary cards explain the bill far better than left's single-color bars with awkward '$ per kWh' labels.
